title: Unified Inference v4 — Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap, Pricing, Release Notes
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Comprehensive product document for Unified Inference v4: goals, requirements, design decisions, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging proposals, and release notes / rollout plan.
body:
Overview:

Unified Inference v4 is the next major release of Redwood's unified serving abstraction that further narrows the gap between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The initiative focuses on simplifying model routing, improving per-request cost controls, and providing a single set of developer APIs and operational primitives across all deployment modes.

Key outcomes (90-day view):
- Single stable API for advanced routing and cost-aware fallbacks.
- 20-30% reduction in per-token cost for common prompt patterns via improved batching + cache heuristics.
- GA of policy-based routing (region/tier/cost) and rollout rules across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Goals:
1) Developer experience parity: expose identical SDK/REST semantics for routing, fallbacks, and rollouts across all deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
2) Cost controls: introduce request-level cost caps, model selection hints, and quantization recommendation integrations.
3) Reliability & predictable performance: tighten P95 latency SLOs and provide better observability for quota and fallback events.

Non-goals:
- No new model training features.
- Not a full rewrite of serving runtime; changes limited to routing, orchestration, APIs, and control plane.

Product requirements (PRD):
A. Core user stories (priority order):
  1. As an app developer, I can define routing policies that choose models by cost band, latency SLO, or region, and the platform will enforce them at request time.
     - Acceptance criteria: policy manifests (YAML/JSON) validate in Console; SDK/REST accepts policy_id on request; console shows policy evaluation per request.
  2. As an SRE, I can set per-tenant cost caps (daily / monthly) and per-request max_cost_usd; requests exceeding budget are rejected or downgraded per policy.
     - Acceptance criteria: quota API, cost cap enforcement at request path, alerting on cap breaches.
  3. As a product engineer, I want automatic model fallback to compatible quantized variants when capacity is constrained.
     - Acceptance criteria: fallback traceable in request logs; 95% of fallbacks occur within 150ms; automatic rollback on quality regression.
  4. As a growth engineer, I can run canary rollouts (percent traffic) with automatic health checks (latency, tokens consumed, quality regression via eval hooks).
     - Acceptance criteria: console rollout page, API for canary percentage, automatic rollback on health breach.

B. Functional requirements (flat list):
- Policy manifest schema v1 (JSON Schema) provided and documented.
- SDK additions: routing.policy_id (optional), request.max_cost_usd (optional), request.priority_hint (low/normal/high).
- Control plane: policy evaluation service with audit logs and metrics (policy.evaluations, policy.fallbacks).
- Observability: per-route cost breakdown, token counts, model variant used, fallback reasons.
- Backwards compatibility: existing API surface must continue to work without changes for customers who do not opt-in.

C. Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLOs (hosted API): P50 < 40ms per-token, P95 < 180ms per-token for n_ctx <= 1024 on typical 8-32 token generation windows.
- Availability: 99.95% regional uptime for hosted endpoints.
- Security: policy manifests stored encrypted at rest; audit trails retained 1 year by default.
- Performance regression threshold: CPU/GPU tail latency must not degrade >5% vs v3 baseline.

Design spec (high level):
1) Architecture components:
- API Gate (existing): validate request, attach policy_id, forward to Router.
- Policy Evaluation Service (new, control-plane): evaluates manifests, returns resolution (model variant, fallback rules, cost caps).
- Router / Orchestrator (enhanced): enforces routing decision, selects serving pool (hosted/dedicated/private-compatible), applies KV/prefix cache hints.
- Observability pipeline: additional telemetry (policy.evaluations, fallback.reason, token_cost_estimate) forwarded to Console and metrics store.

2) Policy manifest (example):
- name: low-cost-apis
- retry_policy: {fallback_order: ["llama-3-8q", "redwood-3-8q"], max_fallbacks: 1}
- constraints: {max_cost_usd: 0.002, p95_latency_ms: 200}

3) API changes (SDK + REST) — minimal additions:
- request.body additions: { "policy_id": "string", "max_cost_usd": "float", "priority_hint": "string" }
- response additions: { "routing": "model-id|variant", "policy_evaluation_id": "string", "fallbacks": ["reason strings"] }

4) Compatibility and private deploy behavior:
- Private deployments will run a local Policy Evaluation Service that syncs manifests from control plane or accepts on-prem manifests.
- Fallbacks across networks disallowed in Private; only local compatible model variants will be used.

5) Data & telemetry schema (table):
| metric_name | description | retention |
| policy.evaluations | count of policy evaluations | 90d |
| policy.fallbacks | count by reason & model | 180d |
| routing.latency_ms | time spent in router | 90d |

Roadmap & themes (Q2–Q4 2026):
- Q2 2026 (MVP): policy manifest v1, SDK flags, basic routing + fallback to quantized variants, observability hooks. Target: beta availability to select customers.
- Q3 2026: autoscaling-aware routing, richer rollout controls (canary by identity groups), cost-caps with billing integration, Console rollout UX.
- Q4 2026: GA for Hosted & Dedicated, Private deployment packaging, advanced quality regression detection (prompt-set based).

Milestones and owners:
- Policy Evaluation Service: owner eng-serving-runtime (lead: Priya Nair) — Q2 beta.
- Router enhancements: owner eng-infra (lead: Marco Liu) — Q2–Q3.
- Console UX: owner eng-platform (lead: Sofia Martinez) — Q3.
- Pricing integration & billing hooks: owner finance-and-legal (lead: Rachel Kim) — Q3.

Pricing & packaging notes (proposal):
- Pricing principle: keep unit economics transparent; charge for model compute (tokens) + policy evaluation minimal fixed fee for high-frequency policy usage.
- Proposed changes for v4:
  - Introduce "policy evaluation" tier: first 100k evaluations / month free; $0.00001 per evaluation thereafter.
  - Request-level cost cap feature as an add-on for enterprise customers: $X/month per tenant (negotiable).
  - No change to baseline per-token pricing for existing customers; recommend discounted reserved capacity rates for Dedicated if customers use policy-aware routing aggressively.

Example pricing scenarios:
- Small app (100k requests/month): likely within free eval tier; no change.
- High-frequency programmatic requests (10M requests/month): extra eval costs potentially $100/month; recommend batching + local eval caching to minimize.

Release notes (draft for v4.0-beta):
- New: Policy-based routing (policy manifests, SDK flag policy_id).
- New: Per-request max_cost_usd and priority_hint fields.
- New: Console views for policy evaluations and fallback traces.
- Improved: Router now prefers quantized model variants by default under model-compatibility policies, reducing median token cost by ~22% in internal benchmarks.
- Known issues: quality regression detection is limited in beta; some edge cases where fallbacks may increase latency (tracked under ENG-4621).

Rollout plan and operational playbook:
1) Beta rollout (2 weeks to select customers):
  - Week 0: internal dogfooding + runbook validation; create health dashboards and alerting (policy.evaluations error rate, fallback rate > 5%).
  - Week 1: enable for 5 customers (low-risk, opt-in); monitor P95 latency, fallback frequency, cost deltas; run weekly QBRs with pilot customers.
  - Week 2: expand to 20 customers, begin closed GA planning.
2) GA rollout (post-Q3 milestone):
  - Gradual enablement with default-off for existing customers; migration guidance and no-ops compatibility guaranteed.
  - Provide tooling to convert common routing rules to policy manifests.

Metrics and SLOs to track post-launch:
- Adoption: number of tenants using policy_id > 500 by Q4 2026.
- Cost delta: median token cost change per-tenant (target <= -15% for targeted workloads).
- Reliability: router P95 latency < 180ms; policy_eval success rate > 99.9%.
- Observability coverage: percent of requests with policy_evaluation_id present > 99%.
